objective: Make the first real N0 run safe to execute on scarce GPU/storage without turning safeguards into a separate validation project.
problem_signals: A smoke corpus and real corpus shared the same path, which could contaminate the training lineage or make a later receipt ambiguous.
The original corpus command could materialize an unexpectedly large public dataset before the first semantic checkpoint had proven useful.
Tokenizer training was not explicitly bound to the exact corpus shard hashes used to create it.
The MLM trainer could checkpoint model files but did not preserve enough optimizer/runtime/corpus lineage to resume an interrupted allocation safely.
A target-runtime failure could still waste GPU time if package, CUDA, tokenizer, or backward compatibility were discovered only after the long run began.
builder_actions: Separated smoke corpus/tokenizer directories from the first real corpus/tokenizer lineage.
Made the first real corpus bounded by accepted characters per source and required an explicit opt-in for intentionally unbounded materialization.
Added a corpus receipt verifier that checks active source-config identity, resolved source revisions, every manifested shard byte count, and every shard SHA256.
Added tokenizer receipts that bind the tokenizer SHA256 to the exact corpus shard hashes and code revision used to train it.
Made MLM checkpoints resumable with Accelerator state and receipts that bind model/config/tokenizer/corpus/code/runtime lineage plus cumulative token counts.
Added a one-command target-runtime smoke that records environment/CUDA state, materializes a sample, trains the native tokenizer, executes a backward model preflight, and emits a hashed PASS receipt.
reusable_builder_procedure: Keep cheap smoke artifacts physically separate from real training artifacts.
Before the first long run, bound data volume so architecture/objective failures can be discovered before storage or compute scales unnecessarily.
Hash data shards before tokenizer/model training and carry those hashes forward into downstream receipts.
Checkpoint optimizer/scheduler/runtime state together with model weights so allocation boundaries do not force semantic retraining from zero.
Run dependency, CUDA, tokenizer, forward, and backward checks inside the actual target runtime before requesting a long GPU allocation.
After the first checkpoint, let measured capability failures decide whether to add teaching data, change objectives, or scale the model.
anti_patterns: Do not use a smoke dataset as the real training corpus merely because the path happens to exist.
Do not materialize an unbounded corpus before checking available storage and the value of the first bounded checkpoint.
Do not accept a checkpoint whose data/tokenizer ancestry cannot be reconstructed from hashes and receipts.
Do not spend scarce GPU time discovering import/runtime errors that a target-runtime smoke can catch first.
Do not convert these integrity checks into a separate multi-judge qualification bureaucracy.
guardrails_retained: No private Elaina payload enters public Git.
No private E0/E-INF/A-SYN gradient is authorized by this operation.
Sol teaching seeds remain owner-authorized and preserved.
Model size remains failure-driven rather than locked to the current approximately 350M reference.
builder_lesson: The best lightweight training pipeline makes the expensive step boring: data, tokenizer, runtime, code, and checkpoint ancestry are already verified before the GPU run starts, and the resulting failures feed directly into the next build decision.
